concept: Socio - Religious Reform Movements in the 19th and 20th CE India
question: Syyed Ahmed Barelvi was the founder of which Muslim Reform Movement?
solution:
The correct answer is Wahabi movement.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__ **

__
 
• The **Wahabi movement** was **centered around Patna**, **Bihar**** **was an **Islamic revivalist movement**, whose stress was to condemn any change into the original Islam and return to its true spirit.
 
• The movement was founded by **Syed Ahmed Barelvi**.
 
• The movement was active since 1820 but in the wake of the 1857 revolt, it turned into armed resistance, a **Jihad against the British**.
 
• Subsequently, the British termed **Wahabis **as **traitors and rebels** and carried out extensive military operations against the Wahabis.
 
• The movement was fully **suppressed after 1870**.
 
• British also introduced the term “**sedition**” in the Indian Penal Code 1870 to outlaw speech that attempted to “excite disaffection towards the government established by law in India”.
 
• The Wahabi Movement was an Islamic revivalist movement and a part of the Indian freedom struggle.
 
• He was inspired by the teachings of Abdul Wahab of Saudi Arabia and Shah Waliullah of Delhi.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Deoband Movement** was started in Deoband in Saharanpur district in Uttar Pradesh. It was launched in 1866 by Mohammad Qasim Nanotavi and Rashid Ahmed Gangohi. Objective: To abolish British rule and restore the Muslim Community by educating them.
 
• In the later years of the 19th century, the **Aligarh movement** was an initiative to set up a system of Western-style scientific education in British India for the Muslim population.
 
• The **Ahmadiyya Movement** was founded in British India by Mirza Ghulam Ahmad (1836-1906), an Islamic reformist and mystic who in 1891 claimed that he was a prophet, revivalist (mujaddid), and the messiah (mahdi) anticipated by Muslims.
